sources.title: Astronomy Engine: JavaScript API documentation
sources.locator: GeoVector, Rotation_EQJ_EQD, Equator, Horizon and SiderealTime
sources.readingDepth: Selected API definitions and coordinate frames read; bundled GeoVector Moon branch inspected
sources.rights: Selected source passages inform original project paraphrases; no full text or source artwork redistributed.
claims: GeoVector returns geocentric J2000 coordinates. Its non-lunar path backdates position and optionally corrects aberration; the bundled Moon branch returns GeoMoon directly. Rotation to true equator of date must match the sidereal-time frame.
Equator is topocentric and applies observer parallax; it is not interchangeable with a geocentric vector.
SiderealTime supplies Greenwich apparent sidereal time in hours.
limitations: API descriptions do not validate this app’s implementation or any astrological interpretation.

sources.title: NOAA: General Solar Position Calculations
sources.locator: Solar zenith equation and Sunrise/Sunset Calculations
sources.readingDepth: Selected altitude/hour-angle equations and sunrise correction read
sources.rights: Selected source passages inform original project paraphrases; no full text or source artwork redistributed.
claims: sin(altitude)=sin(latitude)sin(declination)+cos(latitude)cos(declination)cos(hour angle).
NOAA’s sunrise calculation uses zenith 90.833° for atmospheric refraction and solar-disc size; this differs from a geometric centre at altitude 0°.
limitations: NOAA’s approximate solar model is not used as a general planetary ephemeris here.
Its solar-time hour-angle sign convention must not be copied into a different longitude/rotation convention without checking.

sources.title: GeoPy: calculating distance
sources.readingDepth: Mean-radius definition and spherical/ellipsoidal distinction read
sources.rights: Selected source passages inform original project paraphrases; no full text or source artwork redistributed.
claims: The IUGG mean-radius convention (2a+b)/3 for WGS84 is 6371.0087714150598 km.
A spherical great-circle model differs from an ellipsoidal geodesic model.
limitations: The app’s 6371.0088 km rounded radius is WGS84-derived, not an IAU nominal radius.
A display or scoring radius is not an empirically established range of planetary influence.

sources.title: GeographicLib: WGS84 constants
sources.readingDepth: The two WGS84 constants and units read
sources.rights: Selected source passages inform original project paraphrases; no full text or source artwork redistributed.
claims: WGS84 equatorial radius is 6378137 m; flattening is 1/298.257223563.
Using b=a(1−f), the arithmetic mean radius rounds to 6371.0088 km.
limitations: This does not make spherical line distances ellipsoidal geodesics.
